title_options: Ollama Requests Queue Up? Check Parallel Slots and Latency
Why a Second Ollama Request Waits: Slots, Queue and Latency
Diagnose Ollama Request Queueing from One Response
presentation.title_rationale: The previous headline spent 101 characters on a methodology frame ('measuring why') and a parenthetical year, so the topic and the reader's problem arrived late. The new title front-loads the product (Ollama) and the symptom the reader is searching with (requests queueing), then names the two things the page actually delivers: the parallel-slot setting and the latency split. It promises no speedup, no throughput figure and no vendor score, matches the measured scope (one model, one slot by default, CPU-only host), and at 58 characters it needs no truncation, so no long_title_reason is required.
presentation.visual_purpose: Explains the mechanism the article measures rather than decorating it: a request arrives, waits in the scheduler's pending queue while the single slot is busy, then generation begins; the timeline shows that a queued response's total_duration no longer equals load + prompt_eval + eval, and the leftover is the wait. Labels are design labels only - no measured value is plotted, the footer says it is not to scale, and the article's table carries the nanoseconds. Scope: default one-slot CPU-only behaviour on the measured host, matching the body.
